To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a model for multi-stage energy harvesters which predicts the output power and energy conversion efficiency for a harvesting circuit with N rectifiers.
the maximum efficiency of an N stage RF energy harvester is (2N)−2 and that the output power of a voltage doubler with a load resistance of R and an input power of P is P(2−R/R)−2.
the theoretical energy-conversion efficiency of a multi-stage RF energy harvester with N rectifying stages is given by the following equation: ηmax = 0.5N(N + 1)N + 1 + N(N − 1)N(N + 2)N + 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a theoretical model to evaluate the energy-conversion efficiency of RF energy harvesters with multiple stages of rectification and the application of this model to a voltage doubler circuit operating at 5.8GHz.

the development of a theoretical model for multi-stage RF-to-DC energy harvesters, the validation of this model, and the discussion of the theoretical efficiency of multi-stage RF energy harvester circuits.
developing the theory and design for multi-stage RF-to-dc harvesters.

the theoretical energy-conversion efficiency of an ideal N-stage RF energy harvester is 1/(1+2N).

the model can be used to determine the maximum energy-conversion efficiency of an RF energy harvester with N rectifying stages.

the theoretical efficiency for an RF energy harvester is a function of the number of stages (N) and the ratio of the load resistance to the source resistance, and is a maximum when the number of stages is 1 and when the source resistance is much larger than the load resistance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
for an ideal harvester with a fixed input voltage, there is a maximum efficiency for each number of stages and that this efficiency is achieved at a specific load resistance.

a multi-stage RF energy harvester can achieve an energy-conversion efficiency which is higher than the maximum achievable efficiency of a harvester which has only a single rectification stage, but only if the output impedance of the harvester is matched to the load.
, for the same input power level, the output power of a multi-stage harvester increases as the number of stages increases, while the efficiency decreases.
